correctness.rationale: Pair-cut identity counts each unordered separated pair once using endpoint multiplicity; all partition gaps are half sums of elementary cut gaps. For i∈A, equations F=(x+1)(b-y)+(a-x)y and E=(a-x)+2y(b-y), fractional-linearity in x, and a factored nonnegative polynomial bound give the exact cut extrema. Exchanging a,b establishes the global maximum; K1,1 handled separately. Exact rational verification independently recomputed crossing edge weights for shore sizes up to 8 and all set partitions through 7, including equality. Infinite theorem rests on algebra, not finite enumeration.

value.rationale: The primary literature explicitly leaves equal-treatment perfectness beyond a necessary diameter condition, which gives no discrimination on connected complete bipartite networks. This theorem determines the precise friend-enemy reward transition for all shores, supplies small two-block failure certificates, and reveals order-m imbalance sensitivity against bounded balanced thresholds. This structural exact classification is more than a mere instance evaluation.
